stewart_read: Customer opens with a direct cost objection but the rep never explicitly flips it (e.g., 'what's not affordable is the current bill') — instead pivots to program explanation, which happens to work but leaves the flip on the table.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic: rep may have deliberately chosen to build curiosity with the bill-swap pitch rather than argue the objection head-on, since arguing budget early often backfires.
coaching_implication: Even though the pivot worked here, explicitly naming the objection and flipping it ('the bill you're paying now is the real budget problem') would cement the reframe rather than relying on the pitch alone to do the work.

coaching_implication: Even without the bill in hand, rep could still anchor a specific follow-up time ('I'll call you back tomorrow at 5') rather than leaving it fully open.

stewart_read: Rep asks permission to explain rather than building curiosity through a question tied to the customer's own bill pain — a missed chance to anchor on their AEP Ohio bill before pitching.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read is more supported: the rep hadn't yet captured the bill amount at this point (that comes later at 03:13), so there was no anchor available yet.
coaching_implication: Bill/interest capture should ideally happen before the pitch so the program explanation can be tied directly to the customer's own numbers.
